title: Cost leadership and differentiation
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:34Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The only bank point covering both cost leadership and differentiation is Porter's generic strategies, which is written for the senior Business Management course and uses Porter's framework, so it is pitched at a clearly different depth from this Year 9-10 point, and the other matches cover only differentiation or competitive advantage in general.

draft.title: Cost leadership and differentiation
card: The business works to have the lowest costs in its market. Low costs let it charge low prices and still make a profit.
The business makes its product different from rivals in ways customers value, such as design, quality or service. Customers will pay a higher price for the difference.
A cost leader keeps costs down by buying in bulk, making large amounts, or cutting out extras. A differentiator spends on what makes its product stand out.
The two paths pull in different directions. Low prices attract customers who want a bargain, and a special product attracts customers who want something better.
draft.remember: Cost leadership wins on low costs and prices. Differentiation wins on a product customers see as better.

a.q: Which business is using differentiation to compete?
opts: A bakery that sells sourdough made with rare local grains
A bakery that cuts its prices below every other bakery
A bakery that buys flour in huge bulk orders
A bakery that removes seating to keep its costs low
a.why: The bakery with rare local grains makes its product different in a way customers will pay more for. Cutting prices, bulk buying and cutting costs all aim at lower costs and prices, which is cost leadership.
a.clue: Look for the business that makes its product stand out, not cheaper.

b.q: Tom runs a bike shop in Ballarat. A big chain opens nearby and sells bikes much more cheaply. Tom hand-builds custom bikes and offers free fitting. Which strategy is Tom using, and why?
opts: Differentiation, as customers pay more for custom bikes
Cost leadership, as free fitting keeps his costs low
Differentiation, as he sells bikes at the lowest price
Cost leadership, as hand-building makes bikes cheaper
b.why: Custom bikes and free fitting make Tom's product different and better, so some customers will pay more. That is differentiation. Hand-building and free services add to his costs, so he is not a cost leader.
b.clue: Does Tom win by being cheapest, or by being different?

a.best: A bakery that sells sourdough made with rare local grains

b.best: Differentiation, as customers pay more for custom bikes
